experiments.name: Overnight iron fly ±400, 15:20 → next day 09:20
experiments.hypothesis: Option sellers earn the variance premium overnight: an ATM iron fly sold at 15:20 and bought back at 09:20 next trading day makes money after costs.
experiments.mechanism: Muravyev & Ni (2020, J. Financial Economics) 'Why do option returns change sign from day to night?': delta-hedged index option returns are negative overnight and positive intraday. Cycle 1 matched the intraday half (long straddle gross ≈ +, short fly gross −). Overnight the straddle decays for ~18h (more over weekends) while only the opening gap is realised; intraday buyers then bid options back up.
experiments.novelty: Same structure as the rejected intraday fly (E0002), opposite half of the clock. Prediction made before seeing results: gross positive.
experiments.failure_modes: Rejected if IS net ≤ 0 or PF < 1.15, if a few gap days dominate (ex-top-5 ≤ 0), or if the stress run turns negative.

experiments.name: Overnight long ATM straddle (control)
experiments.hypothesis: Control for the overnight-fly hypothesis: if sellers earn overnight, the overnight long straddle must lose gross.
experiments.mechanism: Muravyev & Ni (2020, J. Financial Economics) 'Why do option returns change sign from day to night?': delta-hedged index option returns are negative overnight and positive intraday. Cycle 1 matched the intraday half (long straddle gross ≈ +, short fly gross −).
experiments.novelty: Mirror of the overnight fly's core; same strikes so the data is shared.
experiments.failure_modes: If this is profitable gross, the day/night mechanism is not what drives cycle-1 results.
